source_name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — English canon list
inspection_and_limitations: Inspected October 2026; the Church’s English canon page is undated. It states 81 canonized books (46 Old Testament, 35 New Testament) and gives grouped/combined titles; it names the “Book of Josephas the Son of Bengorion.” This is evidence for the Church’s stated list, not for every split display row, a modern English edition, completeness, chapter boundaries, or reuse rights. The same page’s prose outside the numbered list says the Ethiopic version includes Baruch and third and fourth Esdras, and says the Ascension of Isaiah was preserved in Ethiopic. These mentions are not separate headings in the numbered 81-entry list; their exact work identities and relationship to grouped Ezra entries are unresolved. Treat them as source-stated leads, not additional entries or verified crosswalks. Follow-up context: prose outside this page’s numbered 81-entry list also mentions Baruch and “the third and fourth Esdras,” and says the Ascension of Isaiah was preserved in Ethiopic. Those statements are not separate headings in the numbered list; keep their relationship to the grouped Ezra entries explicit and do not use them to change the 81-entry count.
archive_status: Primary church-source canon list

source_name: University of Tel Aviv — Ethiopic Bible index (Octateuch and additional Old Testament menu leads)
inspection_and_limitations: The university-hosted Ethiopic Bible index lists Genesis in the Octateuch section and links its chapters. The page describes the Ge’ez text as following August Dillmann’s edition and digitized by Ran HaCohen. The archive stores all 50 chapter source pages locally. This historical edition is not identified as the current official EOTC printed edition. The same public index also visibly lists these additional Old Testament menu labels: Regum; Paralipomena (editor label Grébaut); Ezra (Pereira); Esther (Pereira); Iob (Pereira); Proverbia (Pilkington); Ecclesiastes (Mercer); Canticorum (Gleave); Isaia (Bachmann); Lamentationes (Bachmann); Daniel (Löfgren); Hosea (Fuhs); Ioel; Amos (Pereira); Abdias (Bachmann); Ionas (Löfgren); Michaeas (Fuhs); Nahum, Habacuc, Sophonias, Aggaeus, Zacharias and Malachias (Löfgren); Baruch et Epistola Jeremiae; Tobith; Judith; Siracida; Sapientia Solomonis; Ezrae Apocalypsis; Ezra Graecus; Jubilaeorum (VanderKam and a second menu entry); 4 Baruch; Henoch (three menu entries, including Flemming and Charles); Ascensio Isaiae (Charles). These are transcribed menu labels and edition credits, not verified book crosswalks or evidence of accessible/complete chapter texts. Except for the separately audited local Genesis–Ruth, Psalms, Jubilees, and 1 Enoch packages, item URLs, chapter boundaries, text extent, current availability, and item-specific reuse conditions have not been checked. Do not count a menu entry as reader coverage. Follow-up research recorded 2026-10-25: separate TAU information pages for Ezra, the Ethiopic apocrypha, and the Ascension of Isaiah now provide edition descriptions and selected chapter-access claims (SRC-097–SRC-100). They do not establish complete local chapter inventories, exact EOTC crosswalks, wording, completeness, or permission for unrestricted reuse.
archive_status: Primary-language edition transcription and digital source index

source_name: University of Tel Aviv — Information and Notes: The Octateuch
inspection_and_limitations: Bibliographic note identifies Dillmann’s Veteris Testamenti Aethiopici Tomus Primus / Octateuchus Aethiopicus (Leipzig, 1853–1855). The digitizer reports OCR followed by proofreading/corrections, but warns new typos may remain; the critical apparatus is not included. The note says Boyd’s later 1909 edition stopped after Leviticus. Ethiopic verse numbering was replaced by Arabic numerals, follows the Septuagint, and may have discontinuities where the Ethiopic translation omits a Septuagint verse. Preserve this edition’s numbering; do not treat the transcription as freshly collated. The digitizer explains the visible editorial signs: parentheses mark Ethiopic additions to the Septuagint; square brackets mark omissions supplied according to later Ethiopic manuscripts; paired asterisks mark rare additions by Dillmann. These conventions are not a substitute for the omitted critical apparatus.
archive_status: Edition metadata and transcriber’s limitations
